messages:
agnes-support: FYI customer report — after moving traffic to VPCE-backed NLB we see intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures. They can reach the API from the same VPC via NAT, only fails when going through the interface endpoint. Repro steps attached below.

akash-sre: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and any tcpdump/curl output?

agnes-support: Short repro: 1) customer creates interface endpoint for com.redwood.api in us-west-2, NLB as service target. 2) Route table points to endpoint ENI subnets. 3) Client curl -> 502 intermittently, sometimes returns TLS handshake error.

agnes-support: curl verbose output (sanitized):
```
* Connected to vpce-abc123-xxxx.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
* Issue another request -> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

john-eng: Interesting. That TLS alert suggests a cert or SNI mismatch, or that something between client and Redwood is intercepting TLS and returning an alert. But 502 from our side could be the NLB failing to pass to target. Do we have client-side vs server-side traces?

agnes-support: We ran openssl s_client from client subnet:
```
openssl s_client -connect vpce-abc123-xxxx.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com:443 -servername api.redwood.ai
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
SSL_connect:errno=0
139845...: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
---
No peer certificate available
```

julia-ops: Quick checks: 1) Are the endpoint ENIs in the same AZ as client? 2) SGs on ENI allow 443 inbound from client subnets? 3) Target group healthcheck config (NLB->targets) and whether proxy protocol enabled?

agnes-support: ENIs are in same AZ. SG shows 443 allowed from customer CIDR. Target group healthchecks show healthy. They mentioned enabling Proxy Protocol v2 on the NLB during a partial migration.

akash-sre: Proxy protocol + TLS passthrough + PrivateLink can be a tricky combo. If the NLB uses proxy protocol and targets expect TLS directly, but some intermediate (or client) is also doing SNI rewriting, handshake can break. Also if we require SNI to route to correct cert, the NLB shouldn't be terminating TLS. Need to verify whether the NLB is TLS-listener or TCP listener with TLS termination on targets.

john-eng: On our side, hosted API routes expect SNI "api.redwood.ai" for cert selection. If PrivateLink fronted NLB isn't forwarding SNI (because it's doing TLS termination), we'll get cert mismatch. But the openssl errors suggest the server didn't send a cert at all. Could be the target (our service) rejecting connections that include proxy protocol header unexpectedly, closing connection before handshake. If target sees proxy header out-of-band, it can drop.

agnes-support: Repro test we ran in staging: create interface endpoint -> register endpoint with NLB (TCP listener) with proxy protocol off -> requests worked. With proxy protocol on -> TLS handshake fails immediately.

julia-ops: That aligns: proxy protocol inserts a binary header before TLS handshake bytes; if the backend expects TLS right away it will fail. For AWS NLB, proxy protocol v2 must be supported by backend. Does our runtime accept proxy protocol v2? IIRC we support it but only when configured per-listener.

john-eng: We do support proxy protocol v1 and v2, but it must be enabled in the service config (the runtime will strip header when turned on). For PrivateLink setups we have an extra layer — the device seeing the connection could be the endpoint ENI that forwards straight to the NLB target group. If the NLB is inserting proxy header, our process needs to be started with --enable-proxy-protocol. Are the customer's targets running the version with that flag?

agnes-support: Customer confirmed they enabled proxy protocol on NLB but didn't change their target process flags. They rolled back to disable proxy protocol and saw immediate improvement. However they still see occasional DNS resolution returning the regional NLB hostname instead of the vpce DNS (split-horizon caching?) which leads to egress routing to public ALB and 403s from WAF.

akash-sre: Two separate issues then: 1) proxy protocol mismatch -> TLS/502 failures. 2) DNS split-horizon / caching -> traffic leaking to public endpoints. For 2, check VPC DNS resolution and the Private DNS option on the interface endpoint — if enabled it should override the public name in that VPC. But clients may have local DNS caches (dnsmasq, node caches) or corporate resolvers returning public IPs.

julia-ops: Action items: - john-eng to verify runtime proxy-protocol handling and whether we expose clear errors when header format unexpected. - akash-sre to draft support KB explaining NLB proxy-protocol + PrivateLink caveats and recommended config. - agnes-support to ask customer to flush DNS caches and set host resolver to use VPC DNS only (systemd-resolved / /etc/resolv.conf order).

john-eng: I'll add better logging when proxy header bytes are malformed so we return a clear 400-like error rather than dropping connection. Also will confirm default runtime flags in our AMI/container images used by customers. ETA EOD PST.

akash-sre: I'll prepare a short KB with recommended NLB listener type (TCP with proxy-protocol disabled unless backend configured), explicit steps to enable proxy-protocol on targets (and runtime flag), and DNS validation steps:
```
# verify private DNS:
dig +short api.redwood.ai @10.0.0.2  # should return VPC endpoint IP(s)
# from a pod/node check:
cat /etc/resolv.conf
systemd-resolve --status
```

agnes-support: Customer did confirm disabling proxy protocol fixed their immediate errors. They're happy to follow KB for a permanent migration path. I'll coordinate a follow-up runbook to help them switch to proxy-protocol safely.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-logging-proxyheader-v2 -> staging (john-eng)

john-eng: Deployed to staging, running test harness that simulates proxy header + TLS handshake. Initial results: header parsed correctly when flag on, and handshake proceeds. Will run customer-like traffic pattern to check intermittency.

agnes-support: Thanks team — I'll keep customer updated and will close this slack thread after KB + runbook published. :thumbsup:
